Recipe:
Dutch Oven BBQ Spare Ribs 6-8 Servings Adapted from the kitchen of Bobbi Beagley Jennie's Mom 12&inch; Dutch Oven
§ion;
When Jennie was growing up, her mom used to make a wonderful BBQ Spare Ribs recipe. After we were married, she shared the recipe with us, but when we made it, it turned out totally different. It turns out that instead of using Tomato Paste, like the recipe calls for, she always used Tomato Sauce, so it was runny and didn't taste as good.
Boneless Country Style Spare RibsPork or Beef 4 Lbs.
Tomato Paste3 6-oz. Cans Ketchup1 Cup Apple Cider Vinegar¼ Cup Prepared Mustard2 Tablespoons Brown Sugar¾ Cup
OnionFinely Diced ½
Salt2 teaspoons
Heat Dutch Oven with high heat from the bottom, then add the Spare Ribs and stir them occasionally.
Meanwhile, in a seaparate container, mix all the Sauce Ingredients.
When the Spare Ribs are brown, move the Dutch Oven to medium low heat, pour Sauce over the Spare Ribs, and gently stir until Spare Ribs are all coated in sauce.
Put the lid on the Dutch Oven and simmer, stirring occationally.
Simmer until the Spare Ribs are cooked. (ToDo: Need to verify this takes ≈1 hour.)
CAUTION: If you over-cook the ribs they will begin to fall apart, and you end up with shredded BBQ pork or beef.
When serving the ribs, the extra sauce tastes wonderful over baked potatoes, with a dollop of sour cream.
